newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Thousands of S.Korean protesters clash with police.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of S.Korean protesters clash with police.

text.p: Riot police fired teargas to try to disperse thousands of South Korean workers and students marching in central Seoul on Saturday in protest against a controversial labour law, witnesses said.
They said it was unclear if the marchers had been trying to reach a Seoul cathedral, some four km (2.5 miles) away, where top union leaders are sheltering from arrest.

Armour-plated police vehicles fired volleys of teargas at the protesters, in what has become a regular sight on Seoul's streets since the law was rammed through parliament in a dawn session on December 26 while opposition deputies slept.
The protesters, shouting anti-government slogans and demanding the repeal of the law which allows firms to dismiss workers, pelted police with rocks, witnesses said.
The marchers had been part of a larger crowd holding a protest rally in a Seoul park.
Earlier on Saturday strike leaders holed up at Myongdong Cathedral abandoned calls for indefinite stoppages in protest against the law and said they would limit their industrial action.
